strings.name: Nicolás Maduro
strings.summary: A former bus driver and union activist, Maduro served as legislator, foreign minister and vice president before succeeding Chávez in 2013. His rule coincided with severe economic and migration crises, repression and disputed elections. US forces seized him in Caracas in January 2026 and transferred him to New York; Delcy Rodríguez then led Venezuela. He pleaded not guilty to US drug charges and added torture-conspiracy allegations, with the criminal case still pending at cutoff.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His long leadership of Venezuela, economic crisis and electoral controversies have affected Latin American politics, migration and international relations.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Received secondary schooling before working as a bus driver and union organizer.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Long rule and national crisis
strings.highlights.h1.text: Led Venezuela from 2013 to 2026; policies, economic crisis and disputed elections affected regional migration and international relations.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Custody and US criminal proceedings
strings.highlights.h2.text: Seized by the US in 2026; denied drug and torture-conspiracy charges, with no criminal conviction in this case at cutoff.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Pleaded not guilty to added charges
strings.timeline.t1.text: Entered a not-guilty plea to torture-conspiracy charges; the judge postponed trial to June 14, 2027, a future schedule.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Seized by US forces and transferred
strings.timeline.t2.text: Captured in Caracas and taken to New York for prosecution; Rodríguez subsequently led Venezuela.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Disputed presidential election
strings.timeline.t3.text: Authorities declared him winner; opposition polling-station records indicated a contrary result, intensifying legitimacy disputes.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Claimed reelection amid boycott
strings.timeline.t4.text: Authorities declared victory in an election boycotted by major opposition groups and questioned by many countries.
strings.timeline.t5.title: First won presidential election
strings.timeline.t5.text: After Chávez’s death, authorities declared a narrow special-election victory, disputed by the opposition.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Became vice president
strings.timeline.t6.text: Appointed by Chávez and became central to succession arrangements.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Became foreign minister
strings.timeline.t7.text: Served until 2012, working on the Chávez government’s foreign relations.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Entered National Assembly
strings.timeline.t8.text: Moved from union and political organizing into national legislation, later serving as assembly president.
